az_2_lower_wall.blurb: A small cliff in Palisade Park, a cluster of four little crags up on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains outside Tucson, at roughly 8,200 feet. Six bolted lines run from 5.8 up through the 5.11 range, with three of them at 5.11, so it leans toward intermediate and harder climbers rather than first-timers. Visitors who know both walls rate its lines as tougher and more memorable than those on the neighbouring Upper Wall. Bigger trees keep it shadier than the Upper Wall, and the park as a whole stays far cooler than the valley in late spring. The base sits directly beneath the Upper Wall.

az_lost_wall.blurb: Lost Wall is a modest trad crag in the McDowell Mountains on the edge of Phoenix and Scottsdale. The handful of routes here run from about 5.5 to 5.9, so it suits newer leaders more than hard-men, with edges and cracks to work and the odd bolt. The style is old-fashioned rather than modern. The crag can be spotted from the trailhead lot, though the walk in takes a bit over twenty minutes along a path where signs can confuse. Winter is pleasant here; summer is punishing. The wider McDowell range is mostly granite with a trad focus.

az_top_wall_the.blurb: The Top Wall is a short cliff, around 50 feet, in The Oasis section of Granite Gardens in the Granite Dells near Prescott. Its six routes are a mix of trad and bolted lines, mostly from 5.9 to the low 5.11 range, and several can be top-roped. The wall faces southwest, so it sees shade in the morning and sun through to dark, which suits a quick sunny outing. From the dirt lot you cross the creek by a wooden bridge and then climb switchbacks to reach it, with views opening to the south near the top.

az_north_face_the.blurb: The North Face is the quiet back side of The Lost Wall, in the Granite Dells near Prescott, at the south end of the Constellation Trail. It sees little traffic. The climbing is trad on granite faces with crimps and seams, and routes finish at bolted rappel anchors. Grades here run from roughly 5.6 to the 5.10 range. The north side is usually in shade, and surrounding hills bring the shade on earlier in the afternoon.

az_lower_lost_tower.blurb: Lower Lost Tower is the southeast face of Lost Tower in the Rockfellow Group of East Stronghold, Cochise Stronghold, at about 6,000 feet. The face is roughly 300 feet of featured slab with long pitches, plated and studded with chickenheads. It has six routes, mostly trad, from 5.9 through the 5.10 range with one at 5.12. The face is shaded around midday in winter. It is a committed day: the trail up the Upper Lost Canyon branch takes half an hour to an hour and gains over 1,000 feet.
